text:
maria: Heads-up — planning a combined kernel livepatch + NIC firmware update on az6-gpu-pool (eu-west2) this Wed 02:00-05:00 UTC. Rolling cordon/drain, ~10m overlap windows, estimated capacity reduction ~12-15% at peak. Goal is to fix intermittent TX drops we saw last week and get NIC FW to 2.1.6.

infra-bot: maintenance scheduled: id=maint-az6-2026-03-25, window=2026-03-25T02:00:00Z..2026-03-25T05:00:00Z, approver=maria

kevin: Can we nudge to 03:00-06:00 UTC? Batch jobs tend to finish around 02:30 and we already have a canary job starting at 03:00. Also how long is the expected prefix cache / KV warmup after nodes come back?

maria: Prefer keeping 02-05 to reduce overlap with APAC ramp. Prefix cache warmup: expect ~20-40 minutes to re-populate hot prefixes for large models unless we pre-warm. KV cache should be near-warm for steady-state requests.

jamie: Suggest we do a pre-warm step: after each node uncordon run a short scripted replay of 5k common prefixes (low-risk prompts) to warm caches. That will add ~8m per node but reduces tail latency spikes.

maria: Good call. We'll add pre-warm job to playbook. Draft drain/playbook below:

```
# drain/playbook (short form)
for node in $(cat az6-nodes-to-update.txt); do
  kubectl cordon $node
  kubectl drain $node --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300
  ssh -o BatchMode=yes $node 'sudo snap refresh --channel=stable; sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get -y install linux-livepatch; sudo fwupdmgr update --allow-reinstall'
  # run NIC sanity and netperf
  ssh $node 'sudo /opt/redwood/bin/nic-health-check.sh'
  # uncordon after post-checks
  kubectl uncordon $node
  # trigger cache pre-warm job scoped to node's pool
  kubectl run prewarm-$(basename $node) --image=redwood/prewarm:stable --requests=0.1cpu --limits=0.2cpu --restart=OnFailure -- /bin/prewarm --prefix-list common-prefixes-5k.txt
done
```

olaf: Add a post-update netperf from 3 vantage points (eu-west2, eu-west1, us-east1) and check p99 latency + packet loss. If packet loss > 0.5% sustained for 5m, we abort and rollback NIC FW. Also add egress fallback route to eu-west1 for any pods hitting >50ms latency.

sree: Dedicated customers with pinned GPUs — we should coordinate with account teams now. For pinned nodes we can't live-migrate; propose we offer an optional 1hr credit and schedule their pinned workloads to alternate pools during window if feasible.

ops-oncall: Runbook additions:
- Pager threshold: packet_loss > 0.5% for 5m OR p99 tail increase > 150% for 10m.
- Immediate mitigation: pause remaining node updates, uncordon any recently drained nodes that passed checks, enable egress fallback policy.
- Postmortem owner: olaf (if rollback triggered) / sree (customer comms)

kevin: Rough cost of warmbackfill? Estimate 2-3k USD for extra jobs + prewarm VMs during window. Ok with finance?

maria: Noted — finance OK with up to 5k one-time for this critical fix, but prefer we keep it lean.

infra-bot: reminder: update status page if any Dedicated pool loses >10% capacity for >15m; automatic notification will be posted to #incidents if rolling-failures detected.

jamie: I'll own the prewarm scripts and add canaries. Will put test run in staging Tue 22:00 UTC.

maria: Action items: 1) jamie add prewarm scripts to playbook (by EOD Mon) 2) olaf add netperf + rollback steps (by noon Tue) 3) sree loop in account teams and prepare customer comms (by EOD Mon) 4) ops-oncall add pager and SLO thresholds to runbook (ASAP). If no objections, we ship the window as scheduled. :thumbsup:

kevin: :thumbsup:

olaf: :eyes: will add tests

sree: will ping account leads

ops-oncall: copy that, will update runbook and set escalation path

maria: Thanks team — keeping channel for live updates during the window.
